kind.content: I photograph what the light is willing to show.
Twelve years, four continents, one rule: wait for it. I work with magazines, architects and couples who want pictures that feel like memory rather than proof.

kind.alt: Low-key portrait of a woman lit by a single warm light against charcoal

kind.content: I picked up my father’s camera at fifteen and spent the next ten years photographing the harbour where I grew up, mostly after dark.
After a decade assisting editorial photographers in London and Lisbon, I opened a small studio in Norwick in 2018. It has a north window, a darkroom and a kettle that is never quite cold.
I work slowly and with very little equipment. Most commissions are one camera, two lenses and whatever light is already there. Every client receives one hand-printed silver gelatin print.
